history.dynasty: Kadamba (patron deity); rebuilt under Vijayanagara-era restoration and Maratha patronage
history.summary: Saptakoteshwar was the favoured (kuladev) deity of the Kadamba kings, who featured him on coins and copper plates. The original temple stood at Naroa, Diwar (Tiswadi). It was destroyed during the Bahmani conquest (1352-1366), rebuilt in 1391 by Madhava Mantri, minister of Vijayanagara king Harihara, and destroyed again by the Portuguese in 1540. Fearing destruction, the deity was shifted in 1558 to Narve (then Hindale) in Bicholim taluka, where the present temple was built by order of Chhatrapati Shivaji in 1668 (inscription dated 13 November 1668). Restored 2019-2022 by the Goa Archives and Archaeology Department and reopened February 2022. One of the six revered Shiva temples of the Konkan. Legend: Shiva appeared here to grant the wishes of seven sages who prayed for seven crore years ('sapt' = seven, 'koteshwar' = lord of crores). CSV town correction: the temple is at Narve, Bicholim (North Goa), NOT Panaji as the CSV claims.

name: Shree Saptakoteshwar Temple
town_description: Narve is a historic village in Bicholim taluka, North Goa, about 35-37 km from Panaji and reached via ferry from Divar Island. It is known for its cluster of old temples and rock-cut heritage.
